reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Well-governed versus poorly governed AI
themes.definition: AI is framed conditionally: well-governed it widens access to knowledge and public services, poorly governed it deepens inequality and dependence.
themes.inclusion: Include passages explicitly contrasting AI's benefits and harms depending on governance.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages mentioning AI only as a technology sector of another state.
themes.boundary_cases: Where the harms listed include dependence on foreign rules, also code AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence adds a further layer. Well-governed, it can widen access to knowledge and improve public services.
Poorly governed, it can deepen inequality, expose critical systems, displace workers

themes.label: Dependence on externally designed AI
themes.definition: Concern that developing countries become dependent on AI technologies and rules designed elsewhere.
themes.inclusion: Include warnings about technological dependence or rules imposed by other states or companies.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general access-gap statements without a dependence framing.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements on inequality alone are AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: leave developing countries dependent on technologies and rules designed elsewhere

themes.label: UN Global Dialogue as governance tool
themes.definition: The UN's global dialogue on AI governance is cited as an existing tool, alongside the argument that national legislation alone cannot govern AI.
themes.inclusion: Include references to the UN Global Dialogue or other UN AI mechanisms as answers to AI risk.
themes.exclusion: Exclude calls for governance with no reference to the UN.
themes.boundary_cases: The statement that national law cannot govern a borderless technology also supports AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: we have a global dialogue under this organization on the governance of artificial intelligence

themes.label: Taiwan's AI leadership cited for UN inclusion
themes.definition: AI is mentioned as one of Taiwan's high-tech strengths to argue for Taiwan's participation in the UN system.
themes.inclusion: Include passages citing a third party's AI capability as an argument for its inclusion in international bodies.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages discussing the speaker's own AI policy or AI governance.
themes.boundary_cases: This is essentially a listed mention; it may also be coded AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: Taiwan is a thriving democracy with global leadership in high-tech innovation, semiconductors, AI, biotechnology, renewable energy
She's a serious presence in artificial intelligence and the other technologies that will shape this century

value.rationale: Belize's 2026 speech offers a substantive conditional framing of AI (benefits if well-governed; inequality, worker displacement and dependence if not) and points to the UN AI dialogue, whereas other passages mention AI only as part of Taiwan's technological credentials in a UN-participation argument.
